what_this_is: Governed Phase-2 decisions: for a recurrence family, what the CURRENT primary authority says, what the present-day examinable core is, which answer a candidate should study today, and who independently reviewed that. Phase 1 says what recurs; this says what is true now.
what_this_is_not: Not a recurrence store. It never changes a family, an occurrence or a count. The pinned_at_selection block is a COPY taken at selection time so the validator can prove Phase 1 did not move underneath this work.
the_rule_that_governs_everything_here: MIW Written answers are SITTING-ANCHORED. Every answer must be true as at the date of its own examination sitting, not as at today (TEMPORAL_AND_DONOR_VERIFICATION_PROTOCOL s1). A model_answer may therefore be edited ONLY to fix something that was already wrong at its own sitting -- that is a CORRECTION. Where the framework moved AFTER the sitting, the answer is left alone and the present-day position is carried here, at family level, in present_day_position. That is a MODERNISATION. Collapsing the two would corrupt the past-paper product.

families.current_framework_finding: THE GOVERNING STATUTE HAS BEEN REPLACED ENTIRELY. families.current_framework_finding: THE FRAMEWORK DID NOT MOVE - THE QUESTION'S FRAMING DIED. The printed stem asks what the Manila amendments changed and then, in its second limb, asks a candidate to compare 'the existing chapter III of the STCW 95' with 'the amended chapter III'. That comparison has NO PRESENT-DAY CONTENT: the amendments entered into force on 1 January 2012 and the transitional arrangements that let the earlier standards run alongside them ended on 1 January 2017, so there has been no parallel regime for nine years and the label 'STCW 95' names nothing in force. This is HISTORICAL_TERM_OBSOLETE at the level of framing, not of substance: what the amendments introduced is exactly what a Chief Engineer must know about certification and competence today. The family was therefore resolved by reframing to the successor question and answering it in two limbs, and the split is not a bracket split - the governed join QIJ-0005 records QIF-EM-0068 as a WHOLE_VS_LIMB_RELATION of this family at 0.9667 containment, which is to say the second limb's stem is, on its own, another recurrence family in the corpus. That is objective evidence of two independently examinable concepts. No solved MIW paper answers either limb.
present_day_position: The 2010 Manila amendments ARE the STCW Convention. Adopted 25 June 2010, in force 1 January 2012, transitional arrangements ended 1 January 2017; nothing is grandfathered and the label 'STCW 95' describes nothing in force.

Limb A - the engine-department changes - is answered by CA-EM-0007 in four groups: new certificates and ranks (III/5 able seafarer engine, III/6 electro-technical officer, III/7 electro-technical rating); new and strengthened competences (engine-room resource management, leadership and managerial skill, high-voltage systems, security awareness and designated security duties); fitness for duty (revised minimum rest hours with records, and the alcohol limit of 0.05 per cent blood alcohol or 0.25 mg/l in the breath, plus tightened medical standards); and administration (revalidation and refresher training, quality standards and qualified assessors, simulators and distance learning, approved onboard training, and duties on Parties and companies).

The IGF Code training requirements in regulation V/3 and section A-V/3 are NOT part of the Manila package: they were added by resolution MSC.396(95) of 11 June 2015 and came into force on 1 January 2017.

Limb B - onboard training and the standard of competence - is answered by CA-EM-0008. Each chapter III certificate stands on approved education and training, approved seagoing service and the standard of competence in part A of the Code; approved onboard training is structured, recorded in a training record book, supervised and assessed by a qualified person, tied to real work and auditable; and the competence tables have four columns, of which the fourth - criteria for evaluating competence - is what the printed stem asks for by name.
The alternative-fuel training gap is bridged by approved interim GUIDANCE from MSC 110 and MSC 111, which creates no mandatory standard of competence.
future_not_in_force: The comprehensive review of the STCW Convention and Code is in progress at IMO and NOTHING from it is adopted or in force. Its second phase is reported to run to around 2027, with adoption by an extended session of the Maritime Safety Committee or a diplomatic conference; MIW has established no date at source and asserts none. It is the single event most likely to change both limbs of this family, and it is the reason both entries carry a twelve-month review trigger.

The interim guidelines on training for seafarers on ships using alternative fuels and new technologies, and the fuel-specific interim training guidelines for methyl/ethyl alcohol and for ammonia, are approved GUIDANCE. They are not amendments, they create no mandatory standard of competence, and they must not be described as an STCW requirement.
superseded_elements: 'STCW 95' - the Convention as amended in 1995 - describes nothing in force. It was superseded by the Manila text on 1 January 2012, and the transitional arrangements ended on 1 January 2017. The comparison between 'existing' and 'amended' chapter III, which the printed family wording invites and which almost every published note on this subject reproduces, has no present-day content.

independent_review.notes: FIVE checks. THE REFRAMING is the decision that needed most justification, because answering a printed question faithfully is normally the safe course and here it is not. The stem's second limb asks a candidate to contrast 'the existing chapter III of the STCW 95' with 'the amended chapter III'. Reproducing that would teach a candidate to date himself by nine years in front of an examiner, because the transitional arrangements ended on 1 January 2017 and there is nothing left to contrast. The entries reframe and say so explicitly in the body, in the study guides and under superseded_elements, and the examinable substance survives whole. That is the correct handling and the alternative was tested: more literal, less true. THE SPLIT: not a bracket split. QIJ-0005 records QIF-EM-0068 as a WHOLE_VS_LIMB_RELATION at 0.9667 containment, meaning limb B's stem is itself a separate recurrence family - which is external, governed evidence of two independently examinable concepts, and it is the strongest warrant for a limb split anywhere in this tranche. ownership_policy: A family is owned WHOLE (canonical_current_answer) or LIMB BY LIMB (family_current_answers), never both. Ownership is TYPED: the owner_type field decides how owner_id is resolved, so no consumer ever has to infer the kind of answer from the shape of a string. The legacy untyped shape {question_id: ...} still resolves, and resolves to SOLVED_PAPER, because when it was written a solved past-paper question was the only nameable answer in existence -- but R-P2-OWNER-TYPED refuses a library owner written that way, so the fallback can never acquire a second meaning.
